source: curated seed list of real official portals/platforms; every entry starts seed_unverified and is upgraded ONLY by deterministic government-domain verification and/or live credential-free recon. Entries that fail verification stay unreleased.
notes: One family per real platform. A family may serve many destinations, nationalities and jurisdictions — adapters are built per family and reused. No entry may be invented; uncertain platforms are omitted (their routes stay honestly unresolved).

entries.name: U.S. ESTA (Electronic System for Travel Authorization)

actions.purpose: Close the 'DOWNLOAD THE ESTA APP' splash modal that opens on every fresh load of https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/. Its .modal-backdrop swallows all clicks until dismissed. TIMING GOTCHA: the modal's vertical position shifts by ~140 CSS px as its two QR-code images finish loading, so wait for network idle / re-measure the element rect immediately before clicking, or click via element handle rather than a cached coordinate. Verified: selector matches exactly 1 element (text 'CLOSE'); after the click #splashModal computed display went 'block' -> 'none' and .modal-backdrop count went 1 -> 0.

'Start New Individual Application' button inside #what-section on the home page (below the fold, ~y=1410 at 1280x900). Verified: unique id, innerText 'START NEW INDIVIDUAL APPLICATION', click navigated the SPA to https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/disclaimer. EQUIVALENT VERIFIED ALTERNATIVE (above the fold, 2 clicks): CLICK '.btn-group:has(> .create-app-dropdown-menu) > button.dropdown-toggle' then CLICK '.create-app-dropdown-menu li:first-child a' (text 'Individual Application').

'CONFIRM & CONTINUE' in the 'SECURITY NOTIFICATION' modal #confirmModal (DHS system-use notice). CONDITIONAL STEP: it is gated on sessionStorage['estaNoticeAccept'] !== 'true', so it appears exactly once per browser session - on the first Apply click of a fresh context. Treat as optional/if-present rather than a hard-fail step. Verified: appeared on my first pass with #confirmModal visible and buttons #cancelBtn / #confirmBtn; clicking #confirmBtn landed on /disclaimer. On my second pass in the same session it was skipped and sessionStorage read back {'estaNoticeAccept':'true'}.

Disclaimer panel, 'Yes, I have read and understand the information and agree to these terms.' (the 'No' option is #optionsRadios2, which opens an info modal). Verified: after the click input.checked === true and the MDL label gained class 'is-checked'. Side effect: this auto-expands the second accordion panel #2collapseTwo ('panel-collapse collapse' -> 'panel-collapse collapse in'), so #travelRadios1 has a zero-size rect until this step runs.

'The Travel Promotion Act of 2009' panel, 'Yes, I have read and understand the information and agree to these terms.' ('No' is #travelRadios2). Verified: after the click input.checked === true and the NEXT button became actionable. Both radios are MDL custom controls with a 0x0 native input - click the wrapping label / element handle, not the input rect.

'NEXT' at the bottom of /disclaimer. Verified: selector matches exactly 1 element on that page with innerText 'NEXT' (the sibling EXIT button is btn-default). Click navigated to https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/applicantInfo. An invisible reCAPTCHA v3 (textarea[name='g-recaptcha-response']) is armed on this page and passed silently on both of my runs - no visual challenge was presented.

entry_gate.description: UK ETA is app-first: the start URL renders an 'easier on the app' interstitial (React SPA). Click the 'I cannot apply on the UK ETA app.' escape link to the help-downloading page, then 'Continue application online' to the how-to-apply page, then the 'Continue' button, which calls the service's /start/v1 endpoint and hands over to the forms UI at /electronic-travel-authorisation/{session-id}/electronic-travel-authorisation/enter-email-address — the first question of the guest application wizard (GOV.UK one-question-per-page, so exactly one field with a stable id is the expected form-ready state). No login, no account, no captcha on this path.

entry_gate.description: Angular SPA. Landing hero 'Submit e-Arrival' opens a Material dialog offering 'Sign in as Guest' / 'Sign In With Gmail' / QR scan. Clicking the explicit 'Sign in as Guest' anchor (no credentials, creates an anonymous profile) routes straight to the public foreigner individual e-Arrival form at /e-arrival/foreigner/individual-form/draft. Deep links to /e-arrival/* redirect back to / until the guest profile exists, so the click path is mandatory. The two trailing scrolls are settle time: the form is a lazy-loaded module and needs ~5s after navigation before its ~29 Material fields render. If a prior guest session persists in the browser profile the dialog is skipped and the first click navigates directly, which still lands on the same expect_path.

The 'Arrival Card' tile on #/home. entry_gate.description: Landing page -> scroll to footer -> click the stable 'E-Visa Application' footer link (a.footer-link[href="/visa"]) -> /visa, which is the full application wizard (Visa Category / Arrival Information / Personal Information / Passport Information / Review / Attachments) rendered as a single SPA page. No login or account exists anywhere in the flow. IMPORTANT: do NOT use the hero 'Apply Now' buttons — they sit inside an animating carousel (.evisa-courasel-btn) and never pass Playwright's stability check, so clicks time out; the footer link is the deterministic entry. Wizard step 1 (VISA SELECTION) shows a visaType select plus an 'I agree to the terms and conditions' checkbox; the gate deliberately does not tick it (true T&C consent, not an instructions acknowledgment) — visa-type selection and the consent are fill-tier/user actions. All later-step fields (arrivalDate, departureCountry, departureCity, airline, flightNumber, accommodation*, firstName, surname, citizenship, gender, countryOfBirth, dateOfBirth, placeOfBirth, emailAddress, emailAddressConfirmation, phoneNumber, occupation, streetAddress, addressCity, addressCountry, passportType, passportNumber, passportExpireDate, issuingCountry, passportIssuingAuthority) are already present in the /visa page DOM, hidden until their wizard step activates; native inputs are visually masked by custom-styled widgets, so strict is_visible() fails on them — hence the container-based form_ready_selector.

actions.purpose: bring stable footer links into view
open E-Visa Application wizard via stable footer link

entries.name: Uganda e-Visa
entries.operator: Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control (Uganda)

entry_gate.description: From the SME e-Visa landing page, click 'Apply for Visa' in the left nav (#btnOnlineVisa) to expand the application sub-menu, then click the sub-menu 'Apply for Visa' entry (#btnRegister — despite the id, it starts the public application wizard, not an account signup). This lands on /Consulate.aspx, page 1 of the application: a destination-consulate dropdown (#ctl00_contentMain_ddlDestination) plus a Telerik RadCaptcha image-text challenge (#ctl00_contentMain_RadCaptcha1_CaptchaTextBox) that must be answered before Continue advances to the personal-details form. No login or registration exists anywhere in the flow. The captcha is a human handoff; the gate never touches it. The URL carries a timestamp query param (?t=...), so match on path only.

actions.purpose: Expand the 'Apply for Visa' section in the landing-page navigation
Open the application wizard start page (button text 'Apply for Visa'; id is btnRegister but it is the application, not an account signup)

entries.name: South Sudan eVisa
entries.operator: Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration (South Sudan)

entry_gate.description: From eticket.gob.do landing: continue as guest, choose NUEVO ETICKET (lands on /new-request where an invisible Cloudflare Turnstile validates), then CREAR NUEVO creates a new application (an application number is issued) and opens the public form at /Eticket-application. First form step shows the three mandatory migratory questions (leaving DR? / layovers? / DR resident?) as styled radio groups plus a selectbox, with REGRESAR/CONTINUAR wizard buttons. The two SCROLL_TO_BOTTOM steps are deliberate dwell time: CREAR NUEVO stays disabled until the invisible Turnstile on /new-request auto-validates, and clicking too early times out.
